title: A new UNO identity
question: Choose the style to carry through the entire game.

options.label: Comic-card showdown
options.lineage: Comic-strip panels and competitive card-night banter
options.thesis: A lively card game with decisive lettering, strong outlines and four-color accents.
options.viewport: UNO owns the center above three clear play choices; compact original characters frame the action.
options.risk: Heavy outlines can become noisy; keep forms and the live play field quiet.
options.case: Setup becomes a clear roster, menus use compact panels, and real game events trigger brief graphic reactions. Outfit and Barlow stay readable; no copied characters or decorative fake controls.

options.label: Four-color card club
options.lineage: UNO deck packaging and bold tabletop-game graphics
options.thesis: The entire site speaks the same vivid, confident visual language as the cards.
options.viewport: A large UNO title, complete original cast and a centered yellow Play action with distinct Create and Join choices.
options.risk: The familiar card-game language needs disciplined composition to feel distinctive.
options.case: One family of buttons, roster seats, rule selectors and dialogs carries from home into a clear dark arena. Native cards remain the focal point; turn cues and card motion supply the energy.

canonCard.label: Classic game lobby
canonCard.thesis: A conventional game menu with a hero scene and straightforward play buttons.
canonCard.viewport: A familiar centered menu with play modes, settings and a restrained illustrated scene.
canonCard.risk: Clear and familiar, but less distinctive than the two proposed identities.
